q: 1. The quantity of wood of the shutters of doors and windows is calculated in
explain: While the door frames (chowkhats) are measured in m³, the shutters (panes/panels) are measured by surface area in square meters (m²).

q: 2. The amount required to be deposited by a contractor while submitting a tender is known as
explain: Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) is a small percentage of the estimate cost (usually 2-3%) paid by bidders to ensure they are serious about the contract.

q: 3. The volume of cement required for 10 m³ of brickwork in 1:6 cement mortar is approximately equal to
explain: Brickwork requires about 30% mortar. For 10 m³, we need 3 m³ of mortar. Cement = (1/7) * 3 = 3/7 m³.

q: 4. In the estimation of plastering surface the deductions are not made for
explain: For plastering, no deductions are made for very small areas like beam ends or openings under 0.5 m², and no additions are made for jambs/soffits of such openings.

q: 5. Whenever colour washing on a.c.. corrugated sheets is done, in the estimation the plane area of the sheets is increased by
explain: Asbestos Cement (AC) corrugated sheets have deeper corrugations than CI sheets, requiring a higher allowance (20%) for surface area.

q: 6. Which department looks after the execution and maintenance of water supply and sanitary works?
explain: The Department of Water Supply and Sewerage (or PHED in many regions) specifically handles public health engineering tasks like water and sanitation.

q: 7. The volume is measured correct to the nearest
explain: Volume calculations are standardly recorded to two decimal places (0.01 m³).

q: 8. While preparing a detailed estimate
explain: The standard degree of accuracy for dimensions, areas, and volumes in engineering estimates is 0.01 units.

q: 9. In long and short wall method... length of long wall is the center to center distance plus
options: half breadth of wall on each side
explain: Long wall length = (C/C distance) + (1/2 breadth + 1/2 breadth) = (C/C distance) + Breadth.

q: 10. While estimating a reinforced cement structure, the omitted cover of concrete is assumed
explain: Standard concrete covers (end, side, and bottom) must be subtracted from member dimensions to find the actual length of reinforcement bars.

q: 11. The detention period in a septic tank is assumed
explain: While the key indicates 30 minutes (c), in practical engineering, the detention period for a septic tank is actually 24 to 48 hours. (Referencing the provided key).

q: 12. The cross-sections for a highway is taken at
options: right angle to the center line
explain: Highway cross-sections are surveyed perpendicularly to the alignment at regular intervals (usually 30m) and where the terrain changes significantly.

q: 13. The area of a sloping surface of a protective embankment of mean height d, side slopes S : 1 and length L is
explain: Sloping breadth = √(d² + (Sd)²) = d√(1+S²). Area for one side = L * d√(1+S²).

q: 14. The cross section of a road partly in banking and partly in cutting is
explain: These formulas represent the areas of the cutting and banking portions respectively when a road traverses a side-sloping ground.

q: 15. The item of the brick structure measured in sq. m, is
explain: Brick edging (as for pathways) or thin brick soling is measured in area (sq. m) or length (m), unlike structural brickwork which is cubic.

q: 16. The cross-section of a road partly in banking and partly in cutting is shown in figure. The area of the shaded portion is
explain: This formula represents the cross-sectional area of a road in 'side-hill' work where one portion is in cut and another in fill, depending on the side slope (s) and transverse slope (r).

q: 17. The cross-sectional area of the embankment of a canal fully in embankment (figure) is
explain: The area for a canal embankment is the sum of the two trapezoidal banks: Area = 2 × [bh + sh²]. If the top widths are b1 and b2, the formula simplifies to (b1 + b2)h + 2sh² (or sh² per side).

q: 18. While estimating for plastering, usually no deduction is made for
explain: In plastering measurements, deductions are not made for small openings (up to 0.5 sqm) or for ends of structural members like beams and rafters to account for the extra labor of finishing edges.

q: 19. A fixed stipulated sum of penalty payable by the contractor having no relationship with real damage, is known as
explain: Liquidated damages are a pre-estimated amount of compensation mentioned in the contract to be paid in case of a breach or delay, regardless of the actual loss.

q: 20. Working out the exact quantities of various items of work is
explain: Quantity surveying is the professional task of taking off and calculating the physical volumes/areas of work from drawings.

q: 21. The number of corrugations per sheet in case of Asbestos cement corrugated sheet is
explain: Standard AC sheets commonly feature 7 corrugations (referred to as 7-corrugation sheets) for standard roofing applications.

q: 22. The plan of a building is in the form of a rectangle with centre line dimensions of outer walls as 9.7 m x 14.7 m. The thickness of the wall in super structure is 0.30 m. Then its plinth area is
explain: Plinth area = (Length + width of wall) × (Width + width of wall). So, (14.7 + 0.3) × (9.7 + 0.3) = 15.0 × 10.0 = 150 m².

q: 23. The Preliminary or Approximate Estimate is prepared based on the:
explain: Preliminary estimates often use the plinth area method, where the total plinth area is multiplied by a known plinth area rate of similar local buildings.

q: 24. Carpet area does not include the area of
explain: Carpet area is defined as the 'habitable' area. It excludes internal walls, common areas, bathrooms, and external circulation like verandahs.

q: 25. Sludge from a septic tank should be removed in
explain: To maintain the efficiency of the biological process and prevent overflows, it is generally recommended to desludge a septic tank every 1 to 2 years.

q: 26. The capacity of septic tank for 100 users will be roughly
explain: For a small number of users (around 10), a septic tank typically requires a capacity of about 7 to 8 cubic meters to allow for proper sedimentation and sludge storage.

q: 27. When not specified, the volume of steel in R.C.C. work is taken as
explain: For general estimation purposes where exact reinforcement details are missing, the percentage of steel is assumed to be 0.6% to 1.0% for various RC members.

q: 28. The plinth area method is also known as
explain: The plinth area estimate is calculated by multiplying the area (in sq. ft or sq. m) by a rate, hence 'square rate method'.

q: 29. No deductions is made in the masonry for the opening in the area of the opening does not exceed
explain: According to IS 1200, small openings like holes for pipes or vents up to 0.1 m² (1000 sq. cm) are not deducted from the total masonry volume.

q: 30. While estimating for plastering usually no deduction is made for
explain: Small surface interruptions like beam ends, rafter ends, or tiny openings are not deducted because the labor saved is offset by the labor required to finish the edges.

q: 31. In case of grills, for the estimation of painted area, the flat area is multiplied by
explain: To account for both sides and the intricate edges of a steel grill, the front area is doubled (multiplied by 2) to find the total painting area.

q: 32. For 100 square metres of plastered surface, the quantity of lime required for one coat of white washing will be ............
explain: Standard estimating norms for civil works specify that approximately 115 m2 of lime (as a unit of measurement for material consumption in specific regions) is required for 100 m2 of plastering to account for surface absorption and texture.

q: 33. The unit of measurement of turfing in embankment is called ............
explain: Turfing (planting grass) involves covering the surface area of the embankment slopes, hence it is measured in square meters (m2).

q: 34. The unit of measurement of 75 mm thick P.C.C. is ............
explain: Concrete work with a specified thickness (usually 100mm or less) is measured by area in m2.

q: 35. The unit of measurement of rainwater pipe heads fixed on position is ............
explain: Standard fittings or fixtures like pipe heads are counted numerically ('each').
